claims.text:
pareto-front

**Identity / target / source:** `ai:pareto-front` → `ai-pareto-front` → `src/demos/ai/ai-pareto-front`; source `company/domains/proposals/2026-10-18-ai-map-expansion.json#concepts/188`; brief `company/domains/briefs/2026-10-19-ai-next30f.md#14-pareto-front`. **Packet:** O1. **Level / prerequisites:** core; .

**Nearest / distinct payoff:** weighted objective choice is not yet separately registered; this distinguishes finite nondominance from what linear scalarization can recover.

**Computed primary model:** Maximize both coordinates over A(0,4),B(2,1),C(4,0),D(1,.5). D is dominated byB; A/B/C nondominated. Weighted scorew*x+(1−w)*y, w∈[0,1]. ForB to beatA needsw≥.6; to beatC needsw≤1/3, impossible. B is Pareto but unsupported by any such weighting; do not approximate this universal-in-w result with only a slider sweep.

**Countercase / boundary:** MoveB to(2,3): atw=.5 it scores2.5 and beats endpoints2, so a nonendpoint Pareto point can be supported. The feasible set is discrete/nonconvex, all objectives maximized; no claim that every Pareto point in every setting is missed.

**Prediction / transfer recall:** Predict whether every nondominated point wins some linear weighting; recall a feasible point below the endpoints’ tradeoff chord can remain nondominated yet unsupported.

**Intervention / retained witness:** Find front computes all dominance comparisons and weighted winners; moveB computes changed geometry/winner, retaining originalB inequalities. Sweep weights supplements exact interval proof, not replaces it.

**Source obligation:** Declared finite construction and reproduced arithmetic support only this toy. Independently derive every visible claim; acquire an original method body with exact locator before adding generalized performance, history or empirical assertions.
